inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Thanks for confirming that the water supply is on and the tap is fully open' - customer only said the kitchen cold tap flows normally and had not checked any valve

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'The most likely issue is a blocked inlet mesh filter' - hedged, not a confident specific diagnosis

blockingLoop.evidence: Three consecutive turns repeat 'unscrew the fill hose to check the small mesh filter' while ignoring 'the little lever on the pipe the blue hose connects to is at an angle, about half way. Could that be related?' and 'Could I try the half-open lever first?'

rationale: The assistant never explained E17 and, critically, twice ignored the customer's direct report of a half-closed isolation valve on the cold supply right after plumbing work - the actual cause - instead repeating the same inlet-mesh-filter instruction three times after she declined it. It also fabricated that she had confirmed 'the tap is fully open' when she had explicitly said she hadn't checked a valve. Safety wording (unplug, turn off water, towels) was sound and no parts were pushed, but the customer effectively diagnosed the fault herself and got no acknowledgement, so the conversation delivered no useful progress.
